This test's PROBE population additionally requires the EXECUTE grant that makes an endpoint client-reachable, because an endpoint a client cannot call is not an INV-19 question; where the two differ the verdict reports the difference rather than assuming it. What each endpoint must enforce comes from the registry columns authorization_kind and authorization_requirement added by migration 20260919100000. None of those is touched by `create or replace`, so an endpoint that deletes its own capability check stays in this set and fails inside it. THE FLOOR IS GONE: membership is the closure. Completeness is carried by two mechanisms and by neither column being NOT NULL: authorization_kind is a NULLABLE column, the BEFORE trigger client_rpc_registry_declares_authorization REFUSES a mutating STAFF registration that leaves it null, and assert_staff_rpc_authorization_declared() independently DETECTS an undeclared member of the live population -- which is what catches a function that becomes volatile after it was registered. Each endpoint is called twice: once as the negative actor its declaration implies -- for a capability, the role holding the most capabilities among those that do not hold this one, which is what catches a declaration stricter than its implementation -- and once as the DEAN, who holds nothing anywhere. MEASURED AT THIS COMMIT on a clean seeded stack: 31 endpoints, 19 refusing with an error naming the declared requirement and 12 refused earlier. An endpoint that takes a SCOPE is probed against a class this test CREATES inside the same subtransaction as the call and rolls back with it, rather than against whichever fixture row an unordered lookup returned: sharing the briefing fixture's node let one probe collide with the happy-path test on briefings' UNIQUE (institution_id, scope_node_id, created_at), where created_at is now() and now() is constant within a transaction -- an unrelated refusal that hid a planted defect in one CI run and not the next. The split between those two is FIXTURE-DEPENDENT and the verdict reports whichever it measures; the endpoint set is not. REPLACES the mechanism Layer-3 broke as L3-F02: the old set was derived from capability names inside pg_proc.prosrc and a floor of 18 against a population of 21, so deleting one guard removed the endpoint from its own test and the full contract stayed green. BOUNDED: for the 11 refused earlier -- acknowledge_finding, advance_briefing, generate_report, ingest_structured_package, propose_easy_upload_mapping, record_integrity_review, record_question_health_review, review_briefing, revoke_role, transfer_authorize, transfer_execute, transfer_reject, transfer_request, and revoke_certificate where the fixture leaves no certificate the probe's tenant may act on -- refusal is proved but not that it is the declared authorization, because no seeded row lets the probe reach the check. RF-2 is narrowed, not closed.

25 cases on a purpose-built two-department school, covering the three access levels the Management ruling separates and asserting they do not collapse into one. Every row rolled back

every one of the 16 live calculators carries exactly one governing-scope declaration and reads only relations the live catalogue declares -- which since MC-2 are the organizationally scoped sources and the reference band table, so a calculator reaching past its boundary to raw evidence is outside the declared set and is named here. R6. Watched on a plant that restores the institution-flat predicate, which turns exactly four cells red. Every row rolled back

WP2. The Management decision model measured against a real integrity signal on a purpose-built two-department school. THE SIGNAL CREATES NOTHING: no Management record and no outcome exist until a human acts, so nothing here turns an observation into a verdict by crossing a threshold. The authorized referral arrives AWAITING_REVIEW carrying no outcome, anchored at the class the evidence was observed in and naming the learner it is about, and the signal row is untouched -- referenced, never rewritten. Referring twice while open is the SAME referral with ONE audit row; once decided, the same evidence may be referred again, because a later judgement is not a duplicate. Deciding is refused to the institution admin -- who outranks both Management roles and passes containment from the root -- and to the educator, each against their own decision row so that a refusal which wrongly succeeds cannot crash the probe instead of reporting the breach, and each refusal is checked to have moved nothing. Reads obey the same boundary: the sibling's decision is invisible to the head of department and every decision is invisible to a learner. Watched on four plants -- Management authority by rank, an institution-flat referral, the idempotency guard removed, and an audit row written before the authorization check. Every row rolled back

WP5A identity and provisioning authority. PROVISIONING IS INSTITUTIONAL ADMINISTRATION, NOT SENIORITY: a head of department and a dean -- whom WP4 calls Management -- an educator and a learner are each refused both the namespace reservation and the import, because none of them holds CAN_PROVISION_PEOPLE at all. Namespace reservation is case-insensitive IN THE DATABASE and not merely in the function that upcases before writing: the unique index is asserted to be over upper(namespace) and a lowercase value is asserted unstorable, both here in the live gate rather than only in the migration's one-time block -- a plant that moved the index to namespace stayed green until this existed. OPENING, VALIDATING AND PREVIEWING AN IMPORT PROVISION NOTHING, counted across persons, institutional identities, accounts and auth users; the preview states zero accounts activated. AN UNCONFIRMED IMPORT REFUSES TO PROVISION and leaves nothing behind. Confirmed, it issues IDs in this school's canonical form and CREATES NO ACCOUNT AND NO AUTH USER. Row-level idempotency is asked at its source: requesting an identity a person already holds here returns that same one and mints nothing -- the import path alone never exercises this, because each of its rows is a different person, so a plant that removed the Person x Institution key stayed green until this asked directly. ANOTHER SCHOOL'S ADMINISTRATOR, who holds the capability over their own root, cannot reserve this namespace, open an import here, or read, confirm, advance or verify this job, and lists none of its jobs, rows or identities. Reservation, confirmation and completion each appear once on the audit record. Every row rolled back. Restated for BOB-10 (M5b interim): its three-row import records the teacher without a role or a place, since a staff row is now refused at validation.

WP5A's canonical thousand-person power-failure acceptance scenario, run end to end. A 10-row import needs no pilot and completes in one step. A 1,000-row import demands one: validated, previewed and confirmed it enters PILOT_IMPORTING and provisions EXACTLY 50 -- asked for 200 rows at a time, so the pilot ceiling is doing the work rather than the chunk size stopping by luck -- then halts at AWAITING_PILOT_VERIFICATION. RECORD 51 IS REFUSED, and the refusal leaves 50 completed and 950 remaining. A human verifies once; verifying again is a no-op and writes no second audit row. Rows 51-100 commit and then nobody calls again, which is what a closed laptop, a lost network and a dead building all look like to this design, because the browser owns nothing. THE DURABLE STATE THEN READS total 1000, completed 100, remaining 900, pilot verified: those 100 are real people holding real institutional identities and not one row past them has moved off PENDING. RESUMING IS JUST ANOTHER CALL -- the job runs to COMPLETED, the pilot is never verified again and nothing asks for it, the first 100 institutional IDs are identical to what the interruption had already committed, 1,010 people hold 1,010 identities and nobody holds two. Reported progress equals committed rows; a row cannot claim PROVISIONED with no person and no ID behind it; a completed job refuses to advance again and carries exactly one completion and one pilot-completion on the record. Watched on plants that remove the pilot ceiling and that count attempts instead of commits. Every row rolled back

WP6A, measured on a purpose-built school where one educator both teaches and learns. AN EDUCATOR WITH NO ENTITLEMENT IS OFFERED NO LEARNING, and holding EDUCATOR does not change that: entitlement is an ACTIVE enrolment plus an open membership under the assignment's node, and my_learning_assignments reads no role at all. Given ONE legitimate entitlement the same account is offered exactly that course and no other, and is still teaching -- CAN_ASSIGN_LEARNING intact, display_role still EDUCATOR, because a held role wins the coalesce over an enrolment. NO SECOND ANYTHING: the same person, account, auth user and institutional ID -- re-asked and returned identical -- and no new role row; the person count is compared too, because omitting it would let a defect minting a second Person pass while the other four counts stayed put. The educator scores 92% and READS IT THEMSELVES while gaining no authority over any other learner's result. NOBODY ELSE READS IT: not another educator standing over the whole school, not the head of department, not the dean, not the institution admin, not a learner, and not Management through the audited door, which binds the authorizing NODE and therefore sees a learner's academic record rather than a colleague's development -- so no Management-visibility question had to be decided, because the answer is closed by construction. THIS TEST NO LONGER CLAIMS THE EVIDENCE IS ISOLATED. It used to read all sixteen catalogue metrics at the institution root before and after the professional development and call them identical; that was vacuous for every ITEM-scoped metric, because an item metric asked at a node has nothing to find, so have=0 stayed have=0 whether the isolation held or not -- and five real leaks passed through that green. The isolation claim now belongs to F06-P20, which asks each metric at its own governing argument. An unentitled colleague is offered nothing and is REFUSED the course outright, and the entitlement carries no authoring, teaching or administrative authority. The educator then becomes a HEAD OF DEPARTMENT and the evidence is unchanged, still professional development, still theirs. No certificate function knows what a learning context is, so that engine was neither weakened nor duplicated. Watched on plants: a second Person, a second auth identity, a second institutional ID, teaching authority carried by an entitlement, and display_role rewritten to STUDENT. Every row rolled back

WP6A, the isolation claim itself, measured where each metric can actually be measured. SEVENTEEN READINGS, EACH AT ITS OWN GOVERNING ARGUMENT: class metrics at a class, institution metrics at the school, ITEM METRICS AT A REAL ITEM ID, the learner metric read by an educator the catalogue admits about their own student, and the misconception metric asked a second time at the professional-development class where a teacher's practice answer would surface if it leaked. THE ACADEMIC CONTROL IS NON-VACUOUS: a student in the taught class answers the chosen item correctly, so the item metrics hold real evidence and are capable of moving; the item is chosen with an ORDER BY, because an unordered limit measures the harness. THE PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT IS REAL: the same educator answers the SAME academic item wrongly, choosing a distractor that carries a misconception code, in an OFFICIAL session at their own PD class, with a result and a certificate sealed through the ORDINARY machinery -- eligibility, prepare, seal -- because a separate weak PD certificate engine is exactly what must not exist. That evidence is asserted to EXIST and asserted to be ABSENT from academic_responses and academic_certificates, which is the mechanism rather than the symptom, and every one of the seventeen readings is then identical. The educator reads their own PD result; the PD certificate is sealed, unrevoked and verifiable through the ordinary verification route, and is absent from the academic credential source, because certificate validity and academic-metric eligibility are different questions. CONTEXT SURVIVES THE THREE PATHS THAT WERE DROPPING IT: the authoritative creation path establishes the context it is given and defaults to ACADEMIC when asked for nothing; a revision inherits it, and so does a revision of that revision, because editing a course is not a context switch; structured ingestion carries the context the package declares and REFUSES a context it cannot read rather than letting it settle as academic evidence -- each of those run as the administrator, through the CAN_DRAFT gate the product relies on, rather than around it. Watched on five plants, each red naming its own metric or path: response aggregation reading past the academic boundary (item correctness, distractor uptake and position effect), the misconception source reading past it (class and PD misconceptions), PD certificates entering the academic credential source (institution verified credentials), a revision that does not inherit its predecessor's context, and an authoritative creation path that falls back to ACADEMIC. Every row rolled back

WP6A's closure: mutable content produces no committed evidence, and a sealed course's learning context stops moving. The defect this replaces was measured through the ordinary product path with no owner-side write at all -- an educator with CAN_DRAFT authored a course and a release, an administrator with CAN_ASSIGN_LEARNING activated the assignments, a learner sat the assessment, and the course was never sealed, so the same educator could then move its context and take item.correctness_rate from have 1 to 0 and class.misconceptions from a real finding with remediation attached to nothing. THE ENTITLED LEARNER IS NOW REFUSED, AND ENTITLEMENT IS NOT WHAT REFUSES THEM: may_start_assessment still answers OK, and start_learning_session refuses anyway, naming publication, leaving no session row, no result row and no item evidence. The SAME learner, assignment and items are admitted once the release is walked to PUBLISHED by the holders of CAN_FREEZE_RELEASE and CAN_PUBLISH, and the attempt scores and finalizes as OFFICIAL evidence with a result -- so this is a lifecycle rule, not a new refusal. THE SEALED COURSE THEN STOPS MOVING: ACADEMIC -> PROFESSIONAL_DEVELOPMENT is refused by name on a course carrying that learner's evidence, and the item metric is compared as a whole envelope before and after rather than trusting the exception -- identical, and non-vacuous because it holds the answer just recorded. PROFESSIONAL_DEVELOPMENT -> ACADEMIC is refused on a sealed professional-development course and the educator's answers are absent from academic_responses on both sides of the attempt. Revision still inherits both ways on sealed courses; every ACTIVE learning assignment the seeded world already held still binds a startable release, counted before the test builds anything, which is the check that would catch this repair locking out a learner mid-journey; and Quick Assessment's own rule and live-release ordering are read from the function and unchanged. Watched on two plants: removing the learning-cycle release check lets the learner write evidence over editable content, and removing learning_context from the sealed-content guard lets a sealed course be reclassified and its committed evidence reinterpreted. Every row rolled back

Q-12: a learner can DISCOVER a node-scoped assessment they are already authorized to start. An educator launches a Quick Assessment over a class through launch_quick_assessment; the learner of that class finds it through public.my_open_assessments() and through nothing else -- my_learning_assignments() reaches assessment_assignments only through learning_assignment_id and projects PRE_TEST and POST_TEST by name, and the table's own SELECT policy needs CAN_DRAFT or CAN_ASSIGN_LEARNING, which no learner holds; a learner of another institution does not find it; and the discovered id opens a session through the same start_learning_session() every other mode uses, so execution is unchanged. The doorway adds no authority: it returns the unbound assignments may_start_assessment() accepts, which is the predicate start_learning_session() itself calls, so one rule answers both. Every row is rolled back. Watched to fail: removing the may_start_assessment filter makes a learner of another tenant discover it and turns this red.

LOOKING IS NOT COMMITTING. A learner reads an assignment's own pre-start facts -- how many questions, when it closes, whether it pauses, and which attempt this would be -- through public.assessment_orientation(), and reading leaves NO trace: the session count is unchanged, no session exists against the assignment, and no started_at is stamped, so looking has not spent an attempt that is 1 for PRE_TEST and for most POST_TEST and QUICK definitions. Before this the facts were unreachable: assessment_definitions SELECT needs CAN_DRAFT and assessment_assignments needs CAN_DRAFT or CAN_ASSIGN_LEARNING, session_state() returns them but needs a session, and the only thing that makes a session is start_learning_session() -- the commitment itself. assessment_definition_bounds is readable but holds platform bounds per mode (3-60 items), not this assignment's count. Nothing is invented: every column already exists on the definition or the assignment and the set is a subset of what session_state() shows a second later, with closes_at being the same value that becomes the session's authoritative deadline. Authorization is may_start_assessment(), the predicate start_learning_session() itself calls. A learner of another institution and a uuid that does not exist both answer zero rows, so existence is not an oracle (F06-N01's rule on a new surface). Watched to fail twice: dropping the may_start_assessment delegation lets a learner of another tenant read it, and making orientation start a session to answer itself trips the session count, the assignment's session and the attempts-used fact.

THE TOKEN LINT. Every re-set Experience surface in the SOURCE resolves its colours, radii, type sizes and spacing to a token declared in src/app/globals.css -- no raw hex, no rgb(), no Tailwind scale class, no inline pixel. Scope is two declared lists rather than a directory: the surfaces UX-1 has re-set, and the surfaces awaiting their slice with the slice named, and the test fails if any file under src/app or src/components is in neither -- so a surface added later cannot land outside the lint by accident. BOUNDED AND DELIBERATE (Sauron amendment of 2026-09-16 §3): the lint protects the design system, it does not obstruct implementation, so implementation constants -- the A4 sheet's 210:297 geometry, the QR module's square, a computed proportion -- are classified in an allow-list with one line of reason each rather than tokenized, and a stale allow-list entry whose literal has gone fails the test

WCAG 2.1 contrast COMPUTED from the token source file src/app/globals.css: every text token against white, ivory and the well, every status token against those three and against its own soft ground, and the primary's ink against the primary and its hover. Nothing below 4.5:1. This is the test that makes the token lint safe to enforce -- three v1 values failed AA (ink-3 at 2.79 on white, status-ok at 4.33 on its own soft, attention at 4.16 on the well) and a lint that required their use would have enforced an unreadable screen

Every key in the copy table src/lib/hle.ts carries BOTH an Indonesian and an English telling, and a persona override exists in both languages or in neither -- a key that speaks to a learner differently in one interface language is a key that says two things. The internal-word guard, which until now ran for a learner and the public only, is exercised over EVERY persona, both languages and every stage telling a learner can receive; the staff-only allow-list (STAFF_ONLY_PREFIXES) is retained as a scoped statement about audience, and F05-S03 asserts the same declaration from the other side

THE BILINGUAL IDENTITY. The interface language changes rendered text and number formatting and NOTHING ELSE: the learner cycle's read path and the certificate read are driven twice, once per language, through a recording client, and the recorded RPC call sequence and payloads are byte-identical. The structural half stops a later edit from breaking it -- no source file under src/ passes the language into an RPC, a write or a filter, and no migration gives the preference a column. BOUNDED: this drives the application's own call sites through a recording client rather than a hosted session, so it proves what the application ASKS FOR rather than what a live PostgREST receives

Q-11, made mechanical against the SOURCE. The direct certificate-list read requests exactly ten columns -- id, session_id, institution_id, certificate_number, verification_token, status, issued_at_iso, revoked_at, revoked_reason, supersedes_certificate_id -- and every .from('certificates').select(...) in src/ uses that one exported list rather than a second one written inline. signature, key_version, canonical_payload and snapshot_id are named nowhere on a learner surface, so there is nothing on this side of the wire to hide. Also asserts V-6a on the source: no learner page reaches for the service-role issuance route

An ELIGIBLE certificate renders no QR code, no verification link, no copy-link action, no print action, no certificate number and no name-as-issued. Asserted two ways over the SOURCE of src/app/belajar/[tugas]/sertifikat/page.tsx: the binding's own predicates, and the branch order -- the pending state returns before any of the six is built. The binding is applied to my_certificate's result as well as to the list's, because that RPC does not filter by status and returns ELIGIBLE rows. Under the V-6a ruling ELIGIBLE is the default state, not an edge case: certificate_prepare assigns a token and a number to a row verify_certificate refuses, so a link shown here would send a stranger to 'not found' for a certificate the learner was just shown as real

The QR symbol the certificate prints is DECODED BACK to the exact verification link by an independent decoder (jsQR), at three lengths and therefore three symbol versions, and an input past capacity is refused rather than silently truncated. The encoder is in the repository rather than fetched from an image service because a code drawn elsewhere means a URL carrying a learner's verification token leaves PINTAR every time a certificate is rendered; a symbol nobody decoded is a decoration, which is why this test exists rather than a snapshot of the drawing

The application footer in the SOURCE src/components/KakiPintar.tsx carries exactly the four lines supplied -- the responsible person, the legal entity, the email and the domain -- and nothing beside them: no copyright line, no legal claim, no social link, none of which was supplied. The proper nouns are module constants rather than copy-table keys, and the copy table is asserted not to carry them, because a person's name, a company's registered name, an email address and a domain are the same string in both languages and two keys that must never diverge are a divergence waiting to happen. The protocol sits in the href where a browser needs it and out of the visible text where a reader does not, and the external link carries rel=noreferrer so a stranger arriving from a verification link does not announce where they came from. THE HALF THAT MATTERS MOST: no mount that can reach a printed page renders it -- the credential card never renders it at all, and every mount on the certificate page carries pin-noprint -- because a printed certificate carries its ISSUING INSTITUTION's identity, and the software vendor's name on the same sheet would be a second claimant to the provenance of the evidence

THE FOUR SLICE-2 RULINGS OF 2026-09-17, made mechanical against the SOURCE, because each is the kind of thing obeyed on the day it is written and quietly undone six weeks later by somebody fixing something else. (1) LOOKING IS NOT COMMITTING: no page under src/app starts a session while rendering, and the only thing that creates one is a form-submitted server action -- before this slice both assessment routes called startSession() in their render path, so ARRIVING AT THE URL was the commitment and the integrity disclosure could not be shown before the thing it discloses about; a link would also be prefetched by the router and brushed by a thumb, spending the one attempt a PAPER assessment allows. (2) THE ORIENTATION'S AUTHORIZATION IS NOT WEAKENED: assessment_orientation() returns no row when the learner may not begin, and a null reaches the one refusal page rather than a disabled orientation, with no second eligibility opinion computed in this process that could drift from the gate the RPCs use. (3) NO ESTIMATED DURATION AND NONE DERIVED: the Orientation type carries no duration field, the component computes none from item count or hesitation window, and no Slice-2 copy key offers one in either language -- while the two facts that ARE real, the question count and the closing time, are still read and still rendered through the shared compact fact summary so the approved responsive stack reaches them without being restated. (4) Q-15 VERBATIM: both tellings compared byte for byte against the ruled wording, swept for the forbidden register (dipantau, monitored, webcam, screen recording), asserted to render as a paragraph on the well rather than a bordered alert -- which would contradict the words inside it -- and asserted absent from the player, because a disclosure after the commitment is not a disclosure. BOUNDED: this reads the source and the copy table; the database half (the RPC is stable, inserts nothing and spends no attempt) is Bob's terminal verification, not this test's

THE SLICE-2 HOME CARRIES ONE NEXT ACTION AND DERIVES IT, rather than taking the first row of a list. The derivation in the SOURCE src/lib/siklus.ts is pure -- cycle state and lesson progress in, a trail position and a ranking out -- so this drives it through all eleven states a cycle can hold with no database, which is also why it runs in a container where the db facility is absent. The case that earns the test: a Mastery Check finished without a single lesson ever being opened must report as the RESULT, because a cycle is a record of what happened and not a checklist to satisfy in order; a naive left-to-right reading puts that learner back at unread lessons. Also asserts Yazid's ranking (D-088(d), W18: continue before beginning -- a running session outranks everything; then the lesson being read, the chapter whose lessons wait, the Mastery Check whose lessons are read, and a new chapter's mapping last; a finished cycle is never the recommendation and falls to the rest of the list instead of vanishing), that the ordering is total and stable so reversing the input cannot change the answer -- list position by another name -- and that each of the five trail steps renders through the EXISTING cycle.step.* copy keys with the raw enum reaching no reader in either language. BOUNDED: this proves the derivation over the rows the engine returns; it does not prove what the engine returns, and it grants no authority -- may_start_assessment() is still asked separately every time

THE FORM OF ADDRESS, ruled 2026-09-16: natural Indonesian that avoids unnecessary pronouns, and Anda rather than kamu where the reader must be addressed at all. Second person only, and Indonesian only, because the rule is about the reader's pronoun and English has no formal and informal you to choose between. Two halves: every Indonesian telling the copy table renders to a learner or to the public -- THE STAGE OVERRIDES INCLUDED, which is where the informal register survived longest, since a Year 4 telling is exactly where kamu feels natural to write -- and the raw source of every re-set surface, where a hard-coded Indonesian string bypasses the table altogether. A word ending in -mu is read as the informal possessive clitic unless it is one of a DECLARED list of ordinary words that end that way (ilmu, bertemu), so a false positive is fixed in the diff rather than by loosening the pattern. Pending surfaces are excluded by the same declaration the token lint uses, so a surface joins this rule on the day its slice re-sets it. The guard asserts it can still see what it forbids before it sweeps

THE RESPONSIVE FACT STACK, ruled 2026-09-16: a compact fact summary reads left to right across a wide column and stacks label over value on a narrow one, site-wide wherever that structure occurs. Asserted over the SOURCE stylesheet src/app/experience.css, read as CSS rather than as a screenshot, because the defect this prevents is invisible in a wide viewport. THE HALF THAT MATTERS: the guard walks EVERY rule inside the phone block whose subject is .pin-facts, not just the plain class -- .pin-commit .pin-facts outranks .pin-facts at any width, so a stack written only on the plain selector leaves the commitment shell, the screen the correction was raised against, in three columns while the certificate card narrows correctly. The A4 sheet is the one declared exception and is asserted to KEEP its printed row, because 794px of paper is scaled whole and never reflowed, so the viewport's width is not the sheet's width. Also asserts that nothing was added to carry the change -- no generated marker on the pairs -- and that the product's other compact label/value structure, the verification page's rows, narrows the same way, which is what makes this a pattern rather than one fix

The mark the application renders is the SUPPLIED ARTWORK, byte for byte. public/brand/pintar-selalu-logo.png is verified by sha256 against the file Yazid supplied, so a redraw, a recolour, a crop or a well-meant recompression fails -- a digest is the only check that catches the last of those, which looks like nothing and alters artwork somebody else owns. Its intrinsic geometry is read from the PNG header rather than trusted (766x429), so a resize fails even if the digest were updated, and the component's width/height attributes must match it or the reserved box is the wrong shape and the header shifts as the image lands. THE RENDERING CANNOT DISTORT IT: the .pin-merek rule takes its height from a token and leaves width to auto, and the test fails if it ever sets a width, because a squash of a few per cent is not something review catches. AND IT IS NOT ON THE CREDENTIAL: the certificate card references neither the component nor the asset, because a certificate's issuer is the INSTITUTION and a software vendor's mark on the same sheet would be a second claimant to the provenance of the evidence

The institution-mark ruling of 2026-09-17 still holds against the tree. THE Q-7 GAP IS MEASURED RATHER THAN REMEMBERED: the 83 frozen migrations carry no institution-mark or theme column and no public storage bucket, so the day somebody closes Q-7 this fails and points them at the delivery-path half of the problem -- a mark on the public verification page is read by an anonymous stranger, and a column alone does not give them a path to it. BOUNDED BRANDING, NOT TENANT THEMING: no per-tenant theming mechanism has entered the Experience layer, which is the boundary the ruling draws -- an institution may replace the mark and nothing else, because the moment a second thing is configurable per tenant the guarantee that every PINTAR screen behaves the same way for every child is gone. No specific institution is named in src/ (UIN is the ruling's example and belongs in the ruling). And the shell identity has exactly one renderer, so the future substitution has exactly one place to happen

THE EDUCATOR'S TEACHING CONTEXT IS DERIVED, AND NEVER CLAIMED AS A BOUNDARY. `org_nodes_select` and `classes_select` are both is_member_of_institution(...), so the database hands any member of a school EVERY node and EVERY class in it -- a learner included. A heading reading "the classes you may see" over such a list would claim an authorization boundary the database does not draw, which is what the Slice-3 ruling forbids. So the context is derived instead from the reader's OWN role grants: this drives the PURE module src/lib/mengajar.ts through revoked, expired and node-less grants, through the containment predicate that mirrors v_jalur @> array[scope_node_id] including a node's own jalur containing itself, and through a fail-closed empty and null path. THE CASE THAT EARNS THE TEST is the adversarial plant: a class from another department is placed among the rows the query returned, and kelasDalamLingkup must REFUSE rather than filter it out, because a silent drop would let the query filter rot undetected and a stranger's class would then appear under a teaching heading. Also asserts against the SOURCE src/lib/pengajar.ts that the narrowing runs in Postgres (.overlaps on jalur) rather than in this process, that the grant read is narrowed to the reader's own person, that no role NAME appears in the derivation at all -- the thing doc 05 forbids a picker from doing -- and against src/lib/hle.ts that no Slice-3 heading says "boleh Anda lihat"/"you may see" while the replacement names a teaching scope in both languages. BOUNDED: this proves the derivation and the claim; it grants nothing -- every act reached from the context is authorized again by the database

LOOKING IS NOT COMMITTING, ON THE EDUCATOR'S SIDE. The Slice-2 ruling was written for a learner brushing a link and spending their one attempt; the same rule governs a teacher whose next press makes something real for twenty-four children. Asserted against the SOURCE of every page under src/app/mengajar: none writes while rendering -- no insert, update, upsert or delete, and no call to launch_quick_assessment, extend_session_deadline or move_learning_assignment_release -- with the scanner itself watched to catch a planted insert and a planted launcher, because a detector that has stopped detecting reads green forever. The two stages before each commitment are GET renders of the query string (the quick assessment's configure stage is method="get"), so a reload, a prefetch or a back button cannot commit. The only writes in the surface are the two exported server actions in src/app/mengajar/actions.ts, each reached by a form action and asserted NOT to be reachable through an href. Making material available is asserted to be born at DRAFT and activated in its own separate UPDATE -- the statement enforce_assignment_status fires the CAN_ASSIGN_LEARNING check on -- which is also what makes a review page possible at all; RESTATED BY BOB-04 (D-008), this is read where the commitment now lives: the action calls assign_release and never writes learning_assignments itself, and the migration 20261010100000_a_lesson_is_assigned_whole.sql inserts the assignment without a status and activates it in its own UPDATE. And no educator action takes its redirect target from the form, so the learner side's unvalidated `kembali` is not repeated here. BOUNDED: this reads the source; that the database refuses an unauthorized write is the migrations' own property, proved elsewhere

THE QUICK ASSESSMENT'S BOUNDS ARE READ, AND ITS CERTIFICATE SENTENCE IS CHECKED AGAINST THE CONTRACT RATHER THAN AGAINST ITSELF. The item range comes from public.assessment_definition_bounds for QUICK rather than from a literal in the route, the migration's own row is parsed to confirm the ceiling of 20 and the single attempt, and the three minute presets in src/lib/pengajar.ts are asserted to sit inside the 5-to-60 range launch_quick_assessment itself enforces. THE HALF THAT EARNS THE TEST: the reviewed concept told an educator three times that a Quick Assessment does not enter a certificate. mode_policy's QUICK row has certifies = true and its own note reads "evidence is ordinary evidence", so certificate_eligibility does not refuse a QUICK session on mode grounds. This test therefore PARSES mode_policy's column order and its QUICK row out of the migration and requires the copy in src/lib/hle.ts to agree with what it finds: while certifies is true the copy may not deny that the result can reach certificate evidence, may not say the result is not a learner's or is the educator's alone, must actually tell the canonical meaning in BOTH languages (learning evidence, certificate eligibility), and must still say that one Quick Assessment does not issue a certificate -- the opposite overclaim. If a later migration flips that row, this test says the copy has to move rather than quietly becoming wrong. Also asserts the screen promises no per-item result, because responses_select and presented_items_select are CAN_REVIEW_INTEGRITY only and the service statistics views are revoked from authenticated outright

EVERY NUMBER ON THE EDUCATOR'S EVIDENCE SCREEN COMES THROUGH THE METRIC CATALOGUE, AND NOTHING ITEM-LEVEL IS REACHABLE. The metrics src/lib/pengajar.ts asks for are checked against the CATALOGUE SEED parsed out of 20260918100000_metric_catalogue.sql: each must exist and must carry EDUCATOR in allowed_audiences, and an item-level metric is watched to fail that same audience check so the check cannot pass vacuously. No file under src/app/mengajar or in the educator data layer reads responses, presented_items, assessment_results, service_item_statistics, service_distractor_uptake, service_cohort_misconceptions, question health or integrity signals, and none calls recompute_question_health, record_question_health_review, record_integrity_review or terminate_session -- with the forbidden-table scanner watched to catch a planted direct read. class.misconceptions, the aggregate that replaced a concept sentence counting learners against two questions, is asserted to be asked for AND its calculator asserted to carry a misconception code without a person_id or an item_id, so the replacement is not the forbidden read under another name. Absence is first class: a figure renders only on status ok and only when finite, no zero and no `?? 0` stands in for an unknown, and every figure carries the 3-lens action sentence. And the scope line names a class rather than a chapter, because metric_evaluate takes a NODE and every class calculator aggregates that node's official sessions with no release or module filter -- so "Evidence - Class 10A - Chapter 3" was a scope no contract carries. BOUNDED: this reads the source and the seed; what the evaluator returns at runtime is the database's own property

LEARNER NAMES STAY BOUNDED, BARE AND UNJUDGED, AND NO HONORIFIC IS INFERRED. The absence of any source for a Bu or a Pak is READ FROM THE CONTRACT rather than asserted: public.persons is parsed out of 20260912004321_identity_enrollment.sql and shown to carry display_name and no honorific, salutation, title, prefix or gender column, and no migration adds one -- so a greeting that guessed would be guessing about a real person. The copy and the home's greeting composition are then swept for one anyway. Names reach the surface only through memberships -> enrollments -> persons: the test asserts the read is narrowed to the class node, that persons is never fetched in bulk and filtered afterwards, and -- from 20260912004431_authorization.sql -- that persons_select still runs through person_visible_to_me and that its educator branch is still has_scope('EDUCATOR', m.node_id), which is subtree containment. So the name set is bounded by the DATABASE, not by this application, and that is the one set on the educator surface of which that is true. Observation is not judgment: the roster COMPONENT is asserted to have no slot for a pill, a colour, a number or a status and no order but the alphabet, so a screen cannot add one without the component growing a place to put it; the ordering is asserted not to be by anything about the learners; and the copy is swept for tertinggal, bermasalah, malas, failing, at risk, behind, struggling and a dozen more. The neutral sentences are required to be PRESENT rather than merely the harsh ones absent -- "this is a list, not a ranking" and "counts, not judgments", in both languages

THE EDUCATOR COPY IS COMPLETE, DECLARED, BILINGUAL AND FREE OF THE PRODUCT'S INTERNAL VOCABULARY, asserted over the copy table src/lib/hle.ts and the source of every educator surface file under src/app/mengajar. Every mengajar.* key the surface renders is asserted to exist in src/lib/hle.ts, because a missing key renders as the literal angle-bracketed key to a teacher; the one key composed from a value -- the instrument list's mode -- is required to have a telling for every mode it can take. Every declared key is asserted to carry a non-empty telling in both languages in the flat shape F05-S03 and QAC-S01 depend on, and a key whose two long tellings are byte-identical is treated as one that was never translated. The language rule is enforced by ONE pass over the words of every Indonesian telling: a standalone list (kamu, engkau, kau, dikau) plus the -mu clitic with the words that merely end in those letters declared, rather than two patterns that would double-count the same word -- and a planted informal address is watched to be caught, because a sweep that matches nothing reads exactly like a sweep that finds nothing. Anda is required to be present, not merely kamu absent. Finally every telling in both languages is swept for what a teacher must never meet: plp_, role_assignments, scope_node_id, jalur, org_nodes, learning_assignments, assessment_assignments, metric_evaluate, below_minimum, not_permitted, any CAN_* capability, is_ad_hoc, and the lifecycle and mode enums DRAFT, ACTIVE, WITHDRAWN, SUBMITTED, FINALIZED, PRE_TEST, POST_TEST and QUICK

THE SLICE-3 COMPOSITIONS NARROW ON A PHONE, IN DOCUMENT ORDER. Asserted against the SOURCE stylesheet src/app/experience.css, and the ordering half is the point: at equal specificity the later rule wins, so a narrow rule written before the wide rule it overrides is a narrow rule that never happens -- which is exactly the defect that made the orientation facts render as two cramped columns while the test reported them stacked, and why UX1-S0-FAKTA-01 was rewritten to compare document order. Each of the five Slice-3 compositions that cannot hold its shape below 560px (the two-column roster, the action card, the numbered instrument row, the class switcher and the segmented window control) is required to have its wide rule, then a narrow rule AFTER it, and that narrow rule to sit inside a phone media block rather than merely later in the file. The educator's compact fact summaries are asserted to reuse `.pin-facts` so they inherit the approved responsive stack instead of restating it, no educator container redefines that grid, and nothing declared after the last phone block re-widens one. And the quick assessment's live panel is asserted to still carry TWO facts rather than the three the reviewed concept drew: the third was per-item results, which no contract grants an educator, and a silently returning row is how a removed promise comes back

DOES THE BOX FIT, AND IS ANYTHING CLIPPED -- asserted over the SOURCE stylesheet src/app/experience.css and the COMPILED stylesheet in .next/static/chunks. Promoted from a one-off Playwright measurement that found a real defect: four of thirty-two rendered educator pages overflowed at 390px, the worst by 279px, with the document scrolling to 637px inside a 390px viewport. THE FIRST DIAGNOSIS WAS WRONG AND IS RECORDED HERE BECAUSE IT WAS CONVINCING: it read as a missing box-sizing reset making every padded full-width box 48px too wide, and that was an artefact of the measuring harness, which had stripped `@import "tailwindcss"` from globals.css and with it Tailwind's preflight -- the product has had a global border-box all along. Reverting each candidate fix one at a time against the compiled stylesheet showed ONE doing all the work: a button a rule stretches to the width of a phone while `.pin-btn` still tells it `white-space: nowrap`, so the label refuses to fold, the flex column grows to fit it and the panel takes the page's horizontal scroll with it. The guard asserts three things: (I0) the global border-box reset still exists, checked against the BUILT stylesheet rather than assumed, because that is the assumption every padded box in the sheet rests on and losing it breaks all of them at once; (I1) nothing a rule stretches to its container's width refuses to wrap, with a rule counted toward an element only when its selector is a SUFFIX of that element's own -- the first version merged every `.pin-btn` rule into every `.pin-btn` element and let the fix on `.pin-actions .pin-btn` mask the identical defect on `.pin-tugas .pin-tfoot .pin-btn`, reporting green over a real one; (I2) no grid puts a bare `1fr` beside a track holding something that cannot wrap, because the 1fr takes its content as its minimum and pushes the status pill out through a border the surrounding list clips at. WHY THE CASCADE AND NOT A BROWSER: a rendered measurement only covers what some fixture renders, and measured over 44 rendered pages `.pin-op`, `.pin-num-btn`, `.pin-drow`, `.pin-nrow`, `.pin-tugas` and the trail dot matched zero elements -- the defect this guard found on its first strict run was on the learner's home, which no fixture reaches -- and it runs under `npm ci` in CI, where Playwright is not a dependency and no browser is installed. Watched to fail: reverting the wrap treatment turns it RED and restoring it turns it GREEN. BOUNDED: this proves the two shapes that produced measured overflow; emergent overflow from unbreakable content in a fixture nobody has written is not in its reach, and the rendered measurement (32 educator + 56 Slice-1/2 pages at 390px and 1280px, all zero-overflow) is the companion evidence.

The first-login tour is remembered about the PERSON, not the browser, which is the whole reason it is backend state: PINTAR is deployed where one device is shared between learners across a period and one person uses several machines, so localStorage answers the wrong question in both directions. Driven over three INDEPENDENT sessions against public.my_tour_state / note_tour_presented / complete_tour / suppress_tour in the live database -- each session a fresh set of JWT claims, which is what a logout, another browser and another machine all look like from here. Never shown is the ABSENCE of a public.person_tour_state row rather than a guess derived from accounts.created_at, and reading the state creates nothing. Skipping is not a call at all, so a skipped tour is offered again; exactly THREE automatic presentations are given and the fourth is refused by tour_registry.auto_presentation_limit, whose CHECK bounds it at three so no tour can ever declare more; a fourth call to note_tour_presented is a no-op and does not move the count. Dismissal suppresses automatic presentation, completion suppresses it, completing twice keeps the FIRST instant, and a completed tour spends no presentation -- so a deliberate replay that calls the presentation verb by mistake costs nothing. No device-local value is written or read at any point: every answer comes from the database

Shared-device isolation for tour state, over two seeded learners on one connection with everything identical but the session. The second person meets their own state -- offered the tour, count 0, nothing completed -- reads zero rows of the first's under RLS, and cannot reach them by naming their person_id. The attempt is made three ways, weakest to strongest: as the client role straight at public.person_tour_state, where INSERT, UPDATE and DELETE are refused by the absence of any policy for those commands and of any write grant; through the contract, where a signature walk over pg_proc shows NO tour entry point accepts a uuid at all, so there is no argument that could carry a foreign identity; and AS THE OWNER naming another person, which is what every SECURITY DEFINER function is and where RLS does not bind because relforcerowsecurity is false on every public table by design. That last write lands on the SESSION HOLDER rather than the named person, because enforce_tour_state_write derives person_id from current_person_id() instead of trusting the row -- the INV-08 rule applied to a new surface. With no session at all there is nobody to write for and the insert is refused by name

Tour identity, explicit version, and the monotonic guarantee that makes deliberate replay safe. Two declared tours are two rows: finishing learner.first_login leaves educator.first_login untouched, and no role inheritance can change that because nothing in this schema maps a role to a tour -- tour_key is opaque to the backend, so a DEAN cannot inherit the educator tour by construction rather than by rule. A newly DECLARED version of one tour is offered again while version 1 keeps its own dismissal, so a materially new tour re-presents without erasing an earlier decision; and the declaration is a public.tour_registry row that no client role can write -- no non-SELECT policy, no write grant, and a client INSERT refused -- so a version can never be derived from a deployment, a commit, a changed-file count or a copy edit. Replay restores nothing, asserted twice over: NO reset, replay, clear, forget or restart verb exists in public at all, and the attempt made directly AS THE OWNER to clear a dismissal, uncount a presentation, raise the count past the declared limit, move a row onto another version or delete it is refused by the trigger in every case. An undeclared tour answers zero rows and cannot be presented

Tour state is PRESENTATION state and never becomes evidence, asserted structurally against the live schema and then measured. Structurally, through public.assert_tour_state_is_not_evidence(): 35 evidence consumers -- the ten scoring functions, all sixteen catalogue calculators, metric_evaluate, generate_report, both certificate paths, both evidence-class functions, the question-health recompute and the integrity writer -- read neither tour table; no view depends on either; neither carries a session, evidence, mastery, score, result, response, grade, integrity, certificate, institution or enrollment column; person_tour_state has foreign keys to persons and tour_registry and to nothing else; neither table is a declared record class, so transfers_guard refuses to carry it across an institutional boundary by name; neither is a declared metric source, so a calculator reaching for it would fail assert_metric_closure; and no client role holds more than SELECT. Behaviourally: a REAL OFFICIAL result's mastery and its certificate_eligibility verdict are recorded, the same learner is then shown a tour twice, completes it and dismisses another, and both are unchanged to the digit -- with no integrity signal raised against the session and no audit row written, the last deliberately, because INV-18 lists the acts that must be accountable and being shown a tour is not one of them

the source of the first-login tour only looks: no file under src/components/tur, src/app/tur or the two tour libraries navigates, submits or reaches a product RPC; the only writes are the three declared presentation verbs, each validating the key it is handed, and the replay path in the source of Tur.tsx calls none of them
tests.how: src/components/tur/*, src/app/tur/actions.ts, src/lib/tur.ts, src/lib/tur-negara.ts — scanners watched on planted links, pushes, product writes and a replay that spends a presentation

tests.proves: the tour's memory belongs to the person and not to the device: no tour source touches localStorage, sessionStorage, a cookie or IndexedDB; the four RPC signatures are read from the migration that declares them and none takes an identity; the internal version function is revoked from authenticated there; and the presentation cap is read from the person's own row rather than restated in the source
tests.how: src/lib/tur-negara.ts against supabase/migrations/20260922090000_tour_state_follows_the_person.sql — signatures read from the migration; planted localStorage and cookie writes watched

tests.proves: L-1: every value that survives an authentication hop and then becomes a redirect is narrowed to this origin by ONE shipped helper, src/lib/tujuan.ts, which is IMPORTED AND EXECUTED here rather than read as text. Eleven legitimate destinations pass through with their query and fragment intact; twenty-four off-origin shapes are replaced by the caller's fallback -- the network-path //evil.example and its triple- and quadruple-slash forms, both backslash spellings a browser treats as slashes, the same three with a TAB, CR or LF in front (which the URL parser DELETES before parsing, so a check that reads the raw string is looking at a different string), userinfo and encoded-traversal variants, absolute http/https, javascript:, data:, vbscript: and file:. Each refusal is independently confirmed adversarial: the raw form is resolved by the same URL parser NextResponse.redirect will use and required to leave the origin, so a case that proves nothing cannot sit in the matrix unnoticed. THE PLANT RUNS IN-PROCESS: the startsWith('/') predicate this repair replaced is applied to the same matrix and must be shown to ACCEPT destinations that escape, so the test discriminates between the repair and the defect rather than passing against either. Also asserts the caller's fallback is honoured on refusal and NOT applied to a legitimate path, that a missing destination falls back, and that narrowing is idempotent -- what comes out is already the parser's own form, so a second parse downstream cannot read it differently from the parse that approved it

L-1 closure: the four sites that carry a destination across an authentication or action hop -- src/app/auth/callback/route.ts, src/app/masuk/actions.ts, src/app/masuk/page.tsx and src/app/belajar/actions.ts -- each narrow it through tujuanInternal, and none of them still decides with a bare leading-slash test, which is what all four did before. A comment-stripped walk over every .ts/.tsx file under src/ asserts that no OTHER file narrows a destination its own way, so a fifth site cannot be added outside the contract. The helper itself is required to RESOLVE the destination and compare origins rather than pattern-match, because replacing one leading-slash test with a longer list of forbidden prefixes would be the same defect with more lines

L-2: PINTAR 4.0 is institution-provisioned, so magic-link authentication proves access to an identity a school already created and does not create one. The signInWithOtp call carries shouldCreateUser: false -- the Supabase default is TRUE, so the flag's absence was the defect: an unknown address became an auth.users row, and on_auth_user_created then gave it a persons row and an accounts row. No signUp, admin.createUser or inviteUserByEmail call exists in the sign-in actions. AND THE PRIVACY HALF, which is the easy one to get wrong: with creation off an unknown address errors where a known one succeeds, so returning that difference would replace a self-provisioning defect with an account-existence oracle -- the refusal meaning 'no such provisioned identity' is therefore folded into the ordinary outcome and matched on a stable error code, and the actions are asserted to run no database pre-check against accounts or persons and no auth.admin lookup, either of which would rebuild the same oracle one round-trip earlier. The classroom-card path is asserted untouched: still signInWithPassword over deriveCardSecret, with no signup behaviour, so the human PIN has not become an account password

L-2 measured rather than configured: this EXECUTES against the running Auth service and the live schema rather than reading a flag. An address nobody has provisioned asks for a sign-in link exactly as the application asks (create_user: false, the wire form of shouldCreateUser: false), and creates nothing: no auth identity, no PINTAR person, no PINTAR account. Counted BEFORE and AFTER against the live schema, both for that address and as whole-table totals over auth.users, persons and accounts, so the proof is the pair rather than an absence that was always true -- and it is additionally required to have been refused BY THE PROVISIONING GATE, so a broken Auth service that also happens to create nothing cannot pass. The chain being protected is demonstrated in the same run as the plant: an auth.users insert still produces exactly one person and one account through on_auth_user_created -- planted inside a transaction and rolled back rather than exercised against the Auth service, because persons_no_delete means a row created for real could never be removed again, and the test asserts it left no residue. POSITIVE CONTROL, and it asks which gate refused rather than whether mail was delivered: a seeded provisioned address must NOT meet the provisioning gate, and the two addresses must meet different outcomes at it. Delivery is deliberately not asserted -- CI starts the stack with mailpit excluded, so there is no SMTP sink and the send step 500s for any address that reaches it, which is only the provisioned one; an earlier version asserted status < 400 and reported 'the contract refuses everyone' when the contract had let the address through and the runner simply had nowhere to post a letter

The withheld surface renders the canonical ruled sentence and, character for character, nothing else. It is not the statistical absence card and reaches for none of its copy, which appends have/needed on purpose because a readiness floor is a fact a reader may act on and an anonymity floor is the opposite. Watched on plants: a response count smuggled into an open payload neither changes how it is read nor reaches the screen; an appended shortfall is caught by the scanner in both the bracketed and the written-out form; a withheld payload naming some other statement key falls back to the canonical one; a null, an empty object, an unknown state and a published state with no marginals are none of them read as a published snapshot; and an unrecognised state renders nothing rather than its own identifier

the published feedback snapshot is everything that renders and nobody is in it. Its SHAPE is read out of the two places WP7B builds it -- close_feedback_cycle writes the body, feedback_result returns it -- which is also where this asserts the construction carries no person, no respondent and no clock: the assertion that would notice one being added. Rendered, the surface carries the final total, the governed question and the per-option marginals, and the digits on the page are EXACTLY those figures, so no percentage, mean, rank or composite is being computed. A RESPONDENT PLANTED INTO THE PRESENTATION PIPELINE CANNOT SURFACE: names, person ids and a submission timestamp injected at the envelope, the entry and the option are all dropped by the fixed-key projection and reach neither the read nor the screen, with the plant asserted to really carry them. No marginal is a control that leads anywhere. And nothing is aggregated client-side: no feedback file reads the raw response table or the identity-bearing eligibility table or folds rows of its own, no file anywhere under src names the response table, the scanner is shown to catch one, and every endpoint the surface calls is one of the four WP7B registers for clients

the feedback copy is accurate about privacy and is a verdict about nobody. Every label key WP7B STORES has words in both languages -- the five governed questions and four options are read out of the migration -- and the prefix is deliberately NOT staff-only, because a learner reads most of it and exempting it would exempt the questions a child is asked. NO ABSOLUTE ANONYMITY CLAIM survives the sweep in either language, watched on six positive controls, because WP7B accepts a unanimity residual and a privileged-infrastructure residual and a promise that nobody can ever know is a promise it does not make; the copy says the accurate thing instead, that answers are not shown with a name and the teacher receives the class. No database machinery reaches a learner. NOBODY IS SCORED: no telling for any of the three readers names effectiveness, performance, a ranking, a league table, an overall or composite score, an appraisal, a promotion, a sanction, a good or bad teacher, a comparison with other educators or a star, watched on seven positive controls, and no file turns the four-point scale into a figure or orders anything best-first. THE SHEET HAS NOWHERE TO TYPE, with the scanner shown to catch a textarea, and the whole sheet is required including against an option that was never offered. The outcome map is compared with the submission endpoint's own raised sentences in BOTH directions, an unrecognised failure is reported as uncertain rather than as anything definite, a lost-acknowledgement replay is recognised as recorded, and no outcome tells a learner to send again blindly. And no administrator is offered a way in, from their own surface or from anywhere else

W8-01, restated for BOB-08 (a): an institution administrator signed in builds a Bagian, a Tingkat and a Kelas in their own school through BOB-01's structure functions, and the Kelas carries a jalur 6 deep; the same administrator's direct writes to org_nodes and academic_periods are refused (42501); the ladder still refuses a step that is not a step, even to the owner; a dean, an educator and the neighbouring school's administrator are refused. Read from the migration source 20261012100000, which closes the direct write path.

The standing assertion behind W8-01: no table a client may write runs an invoker-rights trigger that calls a function the client cannot execute. It is checked for NON-VACUITY -- the sweep must cover real client-writable tables and real invoker triggers, because an assertion over an empty population is green and says nothing -- and it is owner-run, since a client-executable assertion about client executability would be answering about itself.

An institution assembles a reusable report template from PINTAR's live catalogue and generate_report runs on it. Before WP8 the catalogue, the tables, the capability, the guards and the engine all existed and report_templates held zero rows in every environment, because no product path could write one. The order given is the order kept; each generated entry carries the status the evaluator decided, so authorization still filters per metric; revising makes a new template VERSION rather than an edit in place, and a report already issued still names the version that produced it. The act is audited, and the audit row carries no figure.

The catalogue is PINTAR's and a template only selects from it. A metric of the school's own invention, a visualization the catalogue does not permit for that metric, a template that shows nothing, one that shows thirteen, one assembled for the neighbouring school, and a direct edit of a metric definition are each refused. An institution decides which metrics appear and how they are drawn; it cannot reach what they mean, how they are computed, who may read them or what the minimum sample is.

Authorization is the FIRST gate on the new endpoint, which is RF-2's lesson applied where it is cheap to apply. A dean, an educator and another school's administrator are refused by the capability's name -- and refused by the SAME name when the rest of the call could not possibly resolve: a null metric list, an invented standard report and a template id that does not exist. So the refusal proves authorization rather than a lookup that failed. An anonymous caller is refused too.

Two bounded corrections. A metric retired by a new catalogue version is refused at the moment a template selects it, while a template that named it before the retirement keeps its row -- a catalogue decision does not silently rewrite what a school assembled. And drawable_items_for_definition is no longer granted to a client that could never have used it: it is invoker-rights by design and calls an owner-only function, so a client call could only ever have failed. The assembler still reaches it and a seeded definition still draws its items, so delivery is intact.

A freshly deployed PINTAR can acquire its FIRST administrator, and no second one. Until the release rehearsal nothing could: INV-16 requires an authenticated grantor, forbids self-grant, and lets only an active SYSTEM_ADMIN grant SYSTEM_ADMIN, so an empty database had no door at all. The door added is the operator's alone -- a signed-in session and an anonymous one cannot reach it, by grant and again by the function's own first check -- and it opens only while no active SYSTEM_ADMIN exists. Day zero is reached here by revoking every active SYSTEM_ADMIN through the guard's ordinary revocation path, not by disabling anything. The operator then binds exactly ONE global assignment to an identity Supabase Auth already created; the function creates no identity of its own and refuses when none exists. It is audited under its own action name, it refuses every call after the first, and the session marker it uses is not a key on its own -- setting it by hand while an administrator exists changes nothing. ORDINARY INV-16 IS UNCHANGED: an unmarked unauthenticated grant is still refused, the bootstrapped administrator still may not grant themselves, an institution administrator still may not grant SYSTEM_ADMIN, and that administrator governs the next grant through grant_role like anybody else. AND INITIALISATION IS NOT RECOVERY: success now writes a durable record in platform_bootstrap, and that record -- not the existence of a living administrator -- is what closes the door. Revoking every SYSTEM_ADMIN in the installation does not reopen it, the record refuses UPDATE and DELETE by trigger, and the guard's day-zero clause requires the installation to be uninitialised as well as administrator-less.

A person with no past can be given their first role. The only role-granting surface built its list of people from enrolments, transfers and existing role assignments -- three prior relationships -- so the person who most needs a role, a school's first administrator created moments earlier in Supabase Auth, could not be selected at all, even though grant_role permits the grant and person_visible_to_me already returns true for them to a SYSTEM_ADMIN. persons_awaiting_first_role is the complement of those three sources and nothing wider: a person appears only while they hold no active role, no enrolment and no transfer, and leaves the list the moment they hold any of them, so the union is total and neither half is a directory. It is asserted here that the fresh person is reachable through none of the three sources, that the SYSTEM_ADMIN is offered them by name, that nobody already affiliated appears, that the grant the list exists for is accepted at the institution root, that ordinary onboarding continues from it -- the new administrator builds their own cohort -- and that an institution administrator, a dean, an educator and an anonymous caller are each refused by the SYSTEM_ADMIN name. Visibility was not widened to do any of it: the read defers to person_visible_to_me, and that predicate knows nothing about this list.

A seq conflict and a closed session are told apart by code. The player could not distinguish 'this client_seq is taken, renumber' from 'this session is over', so it either held an answer forever or dropped it. A different answer at a taken client_seq now raises PR001 whose DETAIL is the server's high-water mark for that item, an identical replay is acknowledged, a renumbered answer above the mark is accepted, and an answer into someone else's session raises PR002, the terminal code the player stops on.

Finish declares what the learner gave and the server holds it or refuses. A finish that raced the outbox scored the paper without the answers still travelling. finish_my_session(session, manifest) raises PR006 naming exactly the items whose declared client_seq the server does not yet hold, a seq above the held one is pending too, a malformed manifest is refused, and none of these refusals scores anything; once the answer arrives the same finish succeeds, a repeat returns the same result row, and afterwards an answer and another learner's finish each raise PR002.

An expired session waits out its late-sync window. An answer given before the deadline and received inside late_sync_grace_seconds is scorable (doc 04 §3), so the paper may not be scored the moment the clock runs out: finalize_session raises PR007 while the window is open, a finish without a manifest raises PR007, the transaction-local verified-manifest marker opens only the session it names, an answer held in another session does not satisfy the manifest, and the learner's own satisfied manifest closes the window with both the live and the late answer counted.

A sign-up creates nobody (F-02). Once an installation has an active SYSTEM_ADMIN and no fixtures marker, handle_new_auth_user refuses with PR010 a bare sign-up, a sign-up that wrote a provisioning marker into user_metadata (writable by the signer), an identity naming a person in app_metadata at insert (GoTrue writes the caller's app_metadata only after the insert, so nothing there is a key), an expired activation grant, and the synthetic seed intent on production. What is honoured is a live activation grant, consumed exactly once by an insert shaped as GoTrue makes it (app_metadata carrying only provider/providers, the address in another case), yielding the granted person and not a name the signer chose. The decision is fail-closed (`is not true`); the NULL case this session cannot reproduce is F09-C01's.

A provisioned person can be activated and signs in as themselves (F-01). persons_awaiting_account offers the school's administrator the provisioned person and nobody who already holds an account; another school's administrator, an educator and an anonymous caller are refused, as are an unknown account kind, a malformed email, a card account without a ten-digit card, a card number on an email account, and an institution administrator calling authorize_new_person. The authorized activation is audited once and writes a single-use activation grant; the identity Auth then inserts -- with nothing PINTAR wrote in app_metadata -- is linked through that grant to the provisioned person and activates their PENDING enrolment; current_person_id is that person; the person leaves the list; a second activation is refused; a SYSTEM_ADMIN may authorize a person no institution has provisioned. The same path through the real route and the real Auth service is F09-C02's.

The intake enrols a learner (F-03). The validator accepted role STUDENT and the provisioning step then granted it as a role assignment, which failed every learner row. An import row with role STUDENT now completes, is enrolled (PENDING) in its class through a membership, receives no role assignment, and is who activation offers next.

F-02 on a connection that never set anything (NEW-1). The in-suite test runs on a session that has already set app.seed_intent, where current_setting(..., true) reads ''; GoTrue's connections never set it, and for them it reads NULL, which made the refusal's condition NULL and admitted every real sign-up. On fresh psql connections that never touch the setting -- asserted to read NULL -- with an active SYSTEM_ADMIN and the fixtures marker off, a sign-up shaped exactly as GoTrue inserts it (app_metadata carrying only provider/providers) is refused with PR010, and the same shape is admitted and linked to the granted person when a live activation grant names the address. Rolled back.

Account activation through the real route and the real Auth service (NEW-2). The database suite proved activation with a hand-built auth.users insert, a shape GoTrue never produces, and passed while the product could activate nobody: GoTrue's admin createUser INSERTs the user and writes the caller's app_metadata in a later update, so the trigger never saw the link. Here a signed-in institution administrator activates a provisioned learner by classroom card and a provisioned teacher by email through POST /api/akun/aktivasi, with the fixtures marker off, and the real GoTrue creates both identities. Asserted: /aktivasi offers both; an anonymous caller is refused 401; each identity is linked to the provisioned person (no second person); the learner's enrolment is ACTIVE; each activation grant was consumed once; the learner signs in with the issued card and PIN through the production derivation and reaches /belajar as themselves; a second activation is refused 403. A declared exception to the app runner's black-box rule: the world is built, and the outcome read back, through the database owner, because a provisioned person with no account is a state no seed holds; the act under test is black-box end to end.
